item.title: Cloudflare Updates Clairic Extraction Model and Introduces Lighter Clairic-flash Variant
item.description:
Cloudflare Updates Clairic Extraction Model and Introduces Lighter Clairic-flash Variant

Cloudflare’s Workers AI superintelligence team has announced a major update to Clairic, its frontier AI extraction model, alongside the release of a lighter, faster 9-billion-parameter model called Clairic-flash. Based on feedback from its preview release, Cloudflare redesigned the architecture of Clairic to improve extraction accuracy from complex documents, including images and multi-page PDFs, while maintaining fast performance and open-weights availability on Hugging Face.

🔍 Overview

Cloudflare has transitioned into a neolab building its own frontier AI models for customers and the open-source community. Since announcing the preview of Clairic, the team received extensive feedback on customer use cases, such as extracting data from images of receipts and reading values from support tickets. To excel at reading from unstructured data, the team redesigned the model’s architecture to prioritize highly accurate data extraction.

🧩 How it works

The new architecture introduces several updates to improve extraction performance:

  • Parallel Slot Autoregressive Generation: Instead of a single forward pass, the model now uses parallel slot autoregressive generation for ordinary text and number extraction fields. Each field uses its already written tokens to select the next token and stops at its own end marker. This parallel advancement occurs in the serving batch to ensure fast latency.
  • Specialized Heads: Trained specialized heads handle computation, estimation, forecasts, durations, calculated dates, and explicit arithmetic.
  • Preserved API Features: Despite the architectural changes, the typed API interface still provides confidence scores, character spans, and probabilities with every request.

⚙️ Key details

The updated models offer significant functional improvements over the preview version:

  • Multi-Page and Document Support: The models now support reading complex documents, including PDFs and up to four total images or PDF pages. In a single request, users can extract information such as the supplier, total, and line items (which return as rows preserving the association of description, quantity, and price).
  • Improved Accuracy: On internal benchmarks covering text and images, image reading accuracy improved from 207 errors to 0.
  • Sub-Second Latency: Latency tests measuring complete HTTP responses from self-hosted servers demonstrate response times under one second.

🚀 Availability

Both models are hosted on Workers AI, and their full open weights are available on Hugging Face.

Model Parameter Count Workers AI Endpoint Pricing (per Million Input Tokens)
Clairic 27B @cf/cloudflare/clairic $0.24
Clairic-flash 9B @cf/cloudflare/clairic-flash $0.10

Clairic’s pricing follows System One pricing principles, meaning users are only charged for input tokens, and Cloudflare covers the cost of output token generation.

#Cloudflare #WorkersAI #Clairic #LLM #DataExtraction

Source: An updated Clairic and Clairic-flash are now open-weight, from the new Workers AI Superintelligence team

item.title: Chandra OCR 2: Advanced Document Conversion and Extraction
item.description:
Chandra OCR 2: Advanced Document Conversion and Extraction

Chandra OCR 2, a state-of-the-art OCR model, has been released with significant improvements in math, tables, layout, and multilingual OCR. It converts images and PDFs into structured HTML/Markdown/JSON while preserving layout information.

🔍 Overview

  • Chandra OCR 2 is a state-of-the-art OCR model that converts images and PDFs into structured HTML/Markdown/JSON while preserving layout information.
  • It has significant improvements in math, tables, layout, and multilingual OCR.
  • The model supports 90+ languages and has excellent handwriting support.
  • It reconstructs forms accurately, including checkboxes, and has strong performance with tables, math, and complex layouts.
  • The model extracts images and diagrams, and adds captions and structured data.

⚙️ Key details

  • Chandra OCR 2 has two inference modes: local (HuggingFace) and remote (vLLM server).
  • Multilingual performance was a focus for Chandra 2. There isn’t a good public multilingual OCR benchmark, so the team made their own.
  • The model was benchmarked with the widely accepted olmocr benchmark.

🚀 Availability

  • Chandra OCR 2 is available for commercial self-hosting with a license.
  • For on-prem licensing, contact the team.
  • The Datalab API turns documents into verifiable knowledge your agents act on. Every result traces back to its page and position, and one API can parse, extract, fill and edit documents.
  • Get started with about 5,000 free convert pages every month (work email) — sign up — takes under 30 seconds — or try Chandra in the public playground.
  • If you have high volume workloads, a batch processing service is available that has processed 1B+ pages in a day at peak.

💡 Why it matters

  • Chandra OCR 2’s improvements in math, tables, layout, and multilingual OCR make it a powerful tool for document conversion and extraction.
  • The model’s ability to preserve layout information and reconstruct forms accurately is particularly notable.
  • The availability of a batch processing service for high volume workloads ensures that users can manage their workloads efficiently.

📦 Installation 

1

pip install chandra-ocr

🔧 Usage

  • With vLLM (recommended, lightweight install)
1

chandra input.pdf ./output
  • Print Markdown directly to stdout
1

chandra input.pdf --stdout
  • With HuggingFace (requires torch + transformers)
1
2

pip install "chandra-ocr[hf]"
chandra input.pdf ./output --method hf
  • Interactive Web Viewer (zero extra dependencies)
1

chandra_app

📅 Timeline

  • 3/2026 - Chandra 2 is here with significant improvements to math, tables, layout, and multilingual OCR
  • 10/2025 - Chandra 1 launched

🌐 Multilingual Performance

  • The model supports 90+ languages.
  • Multilingual performance was a focus for Chandra 2.
  • The team made their own multilingual OCR benchmark to test tables, math, ordering, layout, and text accuracy.

📊 Benchmarks

  • Tops external olmocr benchmark and significant improvement in internal multilingual benchmarks.

📄 Document Conversion

  • Convert documents to markdown, html, or json with detailed layout information.

📝 Document Extraction

  • Extracts images and diagrams, and adds captions and structured data.

📋 Form Reconstruction

  • Reconstructs forms accurately, including checkboxes.

📝 Handwriting Support

  • Excellent handwriting support.

📊 Table Performance

  • Strong performance with tables, math, and complex layouts.

#OCR #DocumentConversion #AI #MachineLearning #DataExtraction

Source: datalab-to/chandra

item.title: Amazon Textract Enhances Document Extraction with Custom Queries Adapters
item.description:
Amazon Textract Enhances Document Extraction with Custom Queries Adapters

Amazon Textract has introduced Custom Queries adapters, which allow users to fine-tune the existing fully managed machine learning service to improve extraction accuracy for specific document types, domain-specific terminology, or unique layouts.

🔍 Overview

Amazon Textract is a machine learning service that automatically extracts structured data, layout elements, handwriting, and text from scanned documents. Custom Queries adapters extend the pre-trained deep learning model as modular components to customize output without requiring the user to build custom ML models.

🧩 How it works

To create an adapter, users upload sample documents, annotate them with expected responses and queries, and train the adapter to recognize unique layout patterns. In a production workflow, the process follows these steps:

  • Routing: A lightweight step uses DetectDocumentText to extract raw text and identify the document version via field labels, version identifiers, or form titles.
  • Retrieval: The system retrieves the correct adapter ID from AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store.
  • Extraction: The AnalyzeDocument or StartDocumentAnalysis API is called using the selected Custom Queries adapter.
  • Downstream Flow: Extracted key-value pairs are sent to human review queues, workflow engines, or databases.

⚙️ Key details

Feature Specification
Supported Formats JPEG, PNG, PDF, and TIFF (XFA-based PDFs are not supported)
Sync API (AnalyzeDocument) Processes single-page documents or the first page of multi-page files
Async API (StartDocumentAnalysis) Handles multi-page PDFs and TIFFs up to 3,000 pages
Adapter Limit One adapter per page per feature type per AnalyzeDocument API call

Operational and Security Configurations:

  • Deployment: For production, API calls should be routed through AWS PrivateLink for network isolation.
  • Encryption: Documents in Amazon S3 use server-side encryption; AWS KMS customer managed keys are recommended for production to control access policies and key rotation.
  • Governance: IAM is used for least-privilege access, AWS CloudTrail provides API audit logging, and Amazon CloudWatch handles alerting and operational monitoring.
  • Lifecycle Management: Promotion strategies and solution architecture are adapter-type agnostic, applying to both Tables and Forms adapters.

💡 Why it matters

By externalizing adapter IDs into the AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store, organizations can update production adapter references with zero downtime and no application redeployment. When promoting an adapter to a new environment or training a new version, only the SSM parameter needs to be updated.

While a four-environment span is recommended for production, smaller teams can start with two environments (production and training) in a single AWS account using separate S3 buckets, tags, and naming conventions to isolate workloads.

🚀 Availability

The process for creating adapters currently requires AWS Support tickets. Additionally, while trained model weights transfer, query definitions and training data do not.

#AmazonTextract #AWS #MachineLearning #DocumentAI #DataExtraction

Source: Automating Amazon Textract adapter lifecycle management across accounts | Amazon Web Services

item.title: Two-Stage LLM Pipeline for Product Attribute Extraction
item.description:
Two-Stage LLM Pipeline for Product Attribute Extraction

A new two-stage LLM pipeline has been introduced to extract purchase-discriminative attributes from product catalog text.

🧩 How it works

The pipeline operates in two distinct stages:

  • Stage 1: Discovers a compact, ranked schema of purchase-discriminative attributes for each product category.
  • Stage 2: Extracts attribute values from catalog text using a fine-tuned compact LLM (Qwen3-4B) with Hyper-Parallel Decoding (HPD).

⚙️ Key details

Metric Performance
Extraction Accuracy 85%
Inference Cost Reduction 92% over foundational LLMs

💡 Why it matters

By achieving accuracy on par with the foundational LLM from which it was distilled, this pipeline enables production-scale use for:

  • Product discovery
  • Catalog enrichment

#LLM #ProductDiscovery #Qwen3 #DataExtraction

Source: Scaling E-Commerce Attribute Extraction with Parallel Decoding
